extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, attorneys before the USPTO, and parties involved in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal-discipline proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: A final USPTO Order imposing reciprocal exclusion from practice under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on state court discipline (resignation with discipline pending), describing procedural steps, required notices, duties during exclusion, and path to reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 / § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be predicated upon Respondent's violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), having been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a state (including resignation in lieu of discipline and prohibition from practicing law by a state authority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline is based on the existence of state-imposed discipline (or equivalent resignation with discipline pending) and may mirror the discipline imposed by the state (i.e., identical discipline may be imposed by the USPTO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (procedure per 37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must send a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' by certified mail, notifying the respondent that a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline has been filed and providing an opportunity to file a response opposing reciprocal discipline within forty (40) days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice/Order should identify the state discipline and inform the respondent of the statutory reasons under § 11.24(d)(1) on which they may oppose imposition of identical reciprocal discipline. Proof of mailing/receipt (e.g., certified mail receipt number) documents service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to file a timely response
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent receives the Notice and Order but does not file a response within the prescribed period, the USPTO may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond supports a finding that no genuine issue of material fact exists and that reciprocal exclusion is appropriate; parties should timely assert any defenses or reasons allowed under § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and scope of discipline: exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: The appropriate discipline in this proceeding is exclusion from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO, effective on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exclusion covers practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters until further order; the USPTO may impose discipline identical to the state-imposed sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and reinstatement procedure (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain excluded from practice before the USPTO until the OED Director grants a petition requesting reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is not automatic; the excluded practitioner must file a petition under § 11.60 and obtain the OED Director's grant of that petition to resume practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette containing the respondent's name, registration number, the fact of exclusion, the basis for the discipline (including the predicate state action or resignation), and any admitted violations of rules of professional conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published Notice should state the essential facts of the discipline (e.g., registration number, basis such as resignation with discipline pending, and which rules were admitted violated). Disciplinary decisions are made available for public review in the OED FOIA Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures other jurisdictions and the public are informed of the USPTO action and the underlying reasons for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties while excluded (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded from practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the order references § 11.58 without restating it, practitioners must follow the specific duties set out in that regulation (e.g., notice to clients, transfer of files, accounting for client funds) during the period of exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative dissociation from USPTO systems and customer numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s), if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative steps will be taken to remove the excluded practitioner's association with customer numbers and electronic system accounts to prevent practice through USPTO electronic services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admitted violations of state professional conduct rules as disciplinary predicate
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent admitted in a Petition for Resignation with Discipline Pending to violating Utah Rules of Professional Conduct: 1.3 (diligence), 1.4(a) (communication with a client), 1.15(a) (safekeeping of client funds), 1.15(c) (depositing client funds into a trust account), 1.16(d) (refunding unearned fees), and 8.4(c) (engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions to violating these professional conduct rules served as the factual and ethical basis for the state's discipline and thereby for the USPTO's reciprocal disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for USPTO action: statutory and regulatory citations
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory/regulatory provisions authorize the USPTO to impose reciprocal discipline based on state disciplinary actions; practitioners and OED should cite these authorities when initiating or defending reciprocal disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline by the OED Director
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may file a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' requesting that the Director of the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline upon a respondent identical to that imposed by a state authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complaint initiates the USPTO reciprocal disciplinary process and triggers issuance of a Notice and Order providing the respondent an opportunity to respond within the regulatory timeframe.
